scope: VM pure states, one actual multi-round CPU match, controlled DOM. No new final character animation.

checks.name: Seven explicit presentation states coexist with eleven legacy states and ten commands
R1 victory and defeat remain nonterminal even while the loser is knocked down
Sudden-death first round still waits for actual match completion
All 346 bodies resolve each requested ending without borrowing a death clip for R1
A legacy lose clip is eligible for match loss, never for round loss
Dedicated round pose supersedes only its own state
First match intro is distinct from subsequent round preparation
Double KO and equal-timeout states do not assign a winner
A timeout loser still alive is not promoted to a corpse by decoration
End state masks stale attacking or locomotion flags without writing the actual actor
Presentation tick follows exact round event, pause and backward seek
Repeated round victories restart their clocks through an explicit token
Foreign, stale or copied actors cannot borrow a real match ending
Training, incomplete matches and invalid winners do not create a terminal presentation
Explicit atelier and cinematic pose requests remain independent of live match lookup
CPU match passes R1, resets actors and produces final match states without sampling changing it
Actual Versus uses presentation module and never offers a finisher in nonterminal R1
Atelier exposes reversible R1 poses separately from final ones for real subject links
Twelve gameplay/identity/contract files remain byte-identical to the verified R7 base
